name: General Relief (GR)
agency: LA County Department of Public Social Services (DPSS)
who: LA County resident. Monthly net income under $221 for one person; couple net income limit $375 (DPSS page). Personal property $2,000 or less; cash on hand $100 or less at application ($200 for a couple/family); one vehicle valued $4,500 or less ($11,500 if homeless and living in it); home assessed value $34,000 or less with a lien; not in violation of probation/parole or fleeing prosecution. Age 18+ (U).
benefit: Maximum $221/month for one person (DPSS). Couple grant amount not stated on DPSS page (U). Employable applicants must attend GROW orientation and participate in employment services; benefits limited to 9 months in any 12-month period (U, from 2025 DPSS GR overview).
apply_where: Apply online through BenefitsCal, in person at any DPSS District Office, or request a mailed application packet by phone. Mail to DPSS, P.O. Box 519, Rosemead, CA 91770, Attn: GR Application, or fax to (310) 215-8220.
form: GR application packet (request by phone); GR Information Sheet ABP 392 (rev 07-2021)
status_2026: Active per DPSS page. 2026 amounts not separately confirmed (U).

name: Ability to Pay (ATP) Program
agency: LA County Department of Health Services (DHS), Patient Financial Services
who: Patients receiving care at LA County DHS facilities. Income at or under 200% of the Federal Poverty Level gets care at no cost. Above 200% FPL pays a reduced sliding-scale amount based on family size and income. Dollar cutoffs for 2026 not verified (U). Asset treatment not stated on DHS page (U).
benefit: Free or reduced-cost hospital and clinic care at DHS facilities. DHS states no one will be denied services due to inability to pay.
apply_where: In person or by phone with DHS Patient Financial Services staff (most locations Mon-Fri 8:00 am to 4:00 pm). Application forms and sliding fee scale are linked from the DHS page.
apply_web: DHS Patient Financial Services (coverage and bill help)
status_2026: Active per DHS page. 2026 dollar figures unverified (U).

name: Home-Delivered Meals
agency: LA County Area Agency on Aging (via Nutrition Access LA program)
who: Age 60+ who are homebound due to illness, disability, or isolation. Certain younger adults with a disability who live with an eligible homebound older adult, and spouses or partners of an eligible homebound adult (U).
benefit: Meals delivered to the home. Program is free; participants are asked to donate $1.75 to $3.00 per meal if able (county fact sheet, 2021 version).
apply_where: Call the County of Los Angeles Information and Assistance Line and you will be connected to a local home-delivered meals provider.
apply_web: LA County food and nutrition for older adults
status_2026: Active per county information (U). Fact sheet last updated 2021; waitlists not checked (U).

name: Congregate Meals (senior nutrition sites)
agency: LA County Area Agency on Aging (via local senior and community center providers)
benefit: Free meal at local senior and community centers; voluntary contribution accepted.
apply_where: Walk in at participating sites (some providers accept walk-ins). Call for site information.
apply_web: LA County food and nutrition for older adults

name: Stay Housed LA
agency: LA County Department of Consumer and Business Affairs (DCBA) and partner legal providers (U)
who: LA County renters facing eviction. Income limits not verified (U).
benefit: Free eviction defense legal help, tenant rights services, and homelessness prevention assistance (U).
apply_where: Call the Stay Housed LA line or apply online.
status_2026: Active (U). County FY2025-26 draft recommended $19M for Stay Housed LA; city eviction-defense contract renewed March 2026.

name: Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8)
who: Low-income households within HUD limits and LACDA admission preferences (U).
benefit: Rental subsidy paid to the landlord; tenant pays about 30% of adjusted income (U).
apply_where: General voucher waitlist is closed. Project-based voucher lists are separate and some senior lists are open (U).
status_2026: Closed waitlist. Last general opening about 2022-2023 (U). Reopening date not announced.

name: Healthy San Francisco
agency: San Francisco Department of Public Health (Healthy San Francisco program)
who: SF resident; age 18+; no health insurance; not eligible for Medi-Cal or Medicare; household income at or below 500% FPL (dollar figure not on page). Immigration status and pre-existing conditions do not matter.
benefit: Primary and specialty care through the Healthy SF clinic network. Fees are sliding scale (fee amounts not verified (U)).
apply_where: Self pre-screen and schedule an appointment through the HSF Participant Portal, then meet with a program application assistor at an enrollment site with ID, SF residence proof, and income proof.
status_2026: Active. Enrollment rose about 39% in 2026 after the state froze new Medi-Cal enrollment for undocumented adults (Mission Local, Sept 2026).

name: County Adult Assistance Programs (CAAP)
who: Adults without dependent children with low or no income who cannot work, or who are refugees or immigrants. Residency and income tests apply. Generally ages 18-65 (U). Noncitizens without work authorization are limited (U). SFHSA checks sponsorship with USCIS and notes possible public charge review (U).
benefit: Monthly cash grant, maximum $714/month per SFHSA fact sheet dated March 2026 (U).
apply_where: Apply through SFHSA benefits intake. Call the CAAP line for an application.
status_2026: Active per SFHSA fact sheet dated March 2026. Amount and rules are unverified (U) because the official pages did not fetch.

name: General Relief (GR)
who: Adults with no dependent children; US citizen or documented noncitizen; Orange County resident; must meet income and property limits (amounts not stated on SSA page). Filing an application is the only way to confirm eligibility.
benefit: Cash aid amount depends on application and interview. SSA describes GR as a loan that the county may ask you to repay from a future SSI retroactive award or other funds. Bus passes available for those who need them.
apply_where: Call to schedule the required GR interview (phone interview allowed), visit a select SSA location, or apply by mail. Online application on BenefitsCal ended May 1, 2026.
status_2026: Active, with online application discontinued effective May 1, 2026 (SSA page).

name: Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8)
who: HUD income limits for Orange County (U).
benefit: Rental subsidy paid to the landlord (U).
apply_where: General waitlist closed per an undated city page (U). OCHA posts a notice on its website when it reopens.
status_2026: Closed waitlist (U). Last California opening found was 2023.

name: Valley Medical Center financial assistance
agency: Santa Clara County Health System, Valley Medical Center
who: Gross family income up to 400% FPL, adjusted for family size, after other insurance pays. Full (100%) discount at 0-300% FPL. Facility-only: 75% discount at 301-350% FPL and 50% at 351-400% FPL (hospital guideline effective Feb 2, 2026). Citizenship and residency requirements conflict across sources (U).
benefit: Discounted or free hospital and professional care at Valley Medical Center.
apply_where: Apply through hospital financial counseling with proof of income and household size.
apply_web: Valley Medical Center federal poverty guidelines
status_2026: Active. Hospital FPL table effective Feb 2, 2026.

name: Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8)
apply_where: Voucher waitlist reported closed by a third-party listing (U). SHRA public housing lists are a separate program; an Alder Grove list was reported open via shra.org (U).
status_2026: Closed waitlist per aggregator; not confirmed on SHRA site (U). Average wait about 35 months (U).

name: General Assistance (GA)
agency: Sacramento County Department of Human Assistance (DHA)
who: Adults 18+ with no means of support; Sacramento County residents who intend to stay (U). Employable applicants must be unemployed, working under 100 hours/month, or have a verified disability (U). Grant depends on housing situation and net income (U).
benefit: Monthly cash aid; amount not captured (U). Employable adults limited to 90 days in a 12-month period (U). Applicants sign an SSI/SSP interim assistance agreement; GA is repaid from any SSI/SSP retroactive award (U).
apply_where: In person at a DHA office using the SAWS 1 application (U). Office address conflicts across sources: 1725 28th St, Sacramento 95816, or 2450 Florin Rd, Sacramento 95822 (U). Confirm before going.
status_2026: Active per county pages (U). Board approved GA updates in 2025; 2026 changes not confirmed.

name: Healthy Partners
agency: Sacramento County Department of Health Services (Primary Care)
who: Age 19+; Sacramento County resident; undocumented adults with restricted-scope Medi-Cal; income at or under 138% FPL (county page; current figures unverified (U)).
benefit: Primary care, screenings, lab tests, and prescriptions. Primary care and labs at no cost; most medications at low-cost retail pricing.
apply_where: Call Member Services to enroll. Applications are also available at the Primary Care Clinic, 4600 Broadway, Sacramento (U). Documents: photo ID, Sacramento residence proof, income proof.
status_2026: Unverified. Older county reports mention a waitlist once capacity is reached (U).

name: General Assistance (GA)
who: Adults 18+ (U) with no dependent children, no other means of support, and Alameda County residence of at least 15 days (U). Property and income limits apply; personal property up to $1,000 per 211 listing (U). Immigration status rules conflict across sources (U).
benefit: Up to $336/month for a single person and $548/month for a couple (U). GA is a loan; recipients sign a reimbursement agreement.
apply_where: Apply by phone, online through the county GA portal, or in person at an Alameda County Social Services Agency office. Paper application is Form 90-16.
status_2026: Active. FY2026-27 county budget overview lists $35.6M for GA (U). Grant amounts from undated sources (U).

name: Basic Health Care
who: Adults who do not qualify for Medi-Cal or other insurance. Income limits and exclusions are on the county page and were not captured (U). County notes Jan 1, 2026 changes to Medi-Cal for undocumented adults 19+ (U).
benefit: County-run health coverage for uninsured adults (U). Covered services not captured (U).
status_2026: Unverified. Adult dental coverage for undocumented adults ends July 1, 2026 (county notice, U).

name: Veterans Service Office
agency: Contra Costa County Veterans Service Office
benefit: Free help filing VA disability compensation and burial benefit claims, claim development, case management, and appeals.
apply_where: Walk in or call. Main office: 10 Douglas Drive, Suite 100, Martinez, CA 94553. Richmond branch: 100 37th Street, Room 1033. Hours from third-party listings (U); call ahead.
status_2026: Active (U; hours and branch details from third-party listings).

name: Inland Southern California 211+
agency: Inland Southern California 211+ (nonprofit 211 operator with county contract) (U)
who: Anyone in Riverside County (also covers San Bernardino County).
benefit: Referrals to food, shelter, health, mental health, utility help, job training, and other local services from a database of 3,000+ programs.
apply_where: Call 2-1-1 or the number below. Office at 1835 Chicago Ave., Suite B, Riverside, CA 92506 (U).
status_2026: Active per county 2026 community awards list (3/24/2026). County contract listed through June 30, 2026; renewal not confirmed (U).

name: Share the Care / county oral health referral
agency: County of San Diego HHSA, Local Oral Health Program
who: Low-income and Medi-Cal residents seeking dental care (U).
benefit: Referral to community dental clinics by region (East, Central, South) (U). Free or sliding-scale dental care available at some clinics such as Family Health Centers of San Diego (U).
apply_where: Call the county oral health line for current clinic lists and eligibility (U).
status_2026: Program active per March 2026 county needs assessment (U). Clinic list not verified.
